final_decision.rationale: Multi-step mixed pipeline. Compression excluded by 0%-FP block_boundary. The large darkening is NOT a brightness function — it is the side effect of HSV saturation clipping (sev2), confirmed by per-channel shift signatures on 3 pairs and by explicit brightness-step tests failing (18.6-19.1 dB). Blur is Gaussian σ≈3, confirmed by two independent blur signals and a 1.70 dB win over glass. The flat-sky colourful mottling is additive Gaussian RGB noise (sev≈3) amplified ×6 by the saturation step; flat-patch intensity scaling matches additive (not speckle). Noise type remains the main uncertainty (seed mismatch, blur coupling).

coupling_analysis.saturation_noise_coupling: saturation gain (S×6, sev2) amplifies chroma fluctuations, turning mild additive RGB noise into the strong colourful mottling seen in flat sky; blur before saturation keeps V≤255 (target has ~0% pure-255 values, whereas gamma/shift-darken sims produced 11pp extra 255s → those were rejected).
coupling_analysis.darkening_is_saturation_side_effect: HSV S-scaling leaves V untouched but pushes min/mid channels down, darkening the RGB mean (mean_shift -27..-43) and creating dark clipping (12.7-26.2%). Adding an explicit brightness step over-darkens: blur3+shift_RGB:1+sat2 → 19.11 dB, blur3+gamma_RGB:1+sat2 → 18.63 dB, vs 20.88 dB without → brightness ruled out.

r1_summary.scope: Re-ran run_full_analysis.py on all 5 support pairs (full_analysis_R1_pair0..4.json); noise subtype/severity, blur, saturation, second-order statistics
reanalysis_highlights: 1) Refractory estimator found: R0's noise severity rested on wavelet MAD of the target-clean residual, which returns EXACTLY 1.483 for every candidate (sev2/3/4, YCrCb3, speckle1) - zero resolving power in uint8. Replaced with flat-patch high-pass MAD on clean-defined flat regions (pair0: 1795 patches of 12192; pair1: 807), a seed-robust second-order statistic.

2) Noise subtype = RGB: target flat-patch channel fingerprint R/G=1.04, G/B=0.98, Cr/Cb=1.05 matches RGB sim (1.02/0.99/1.05); YCrCb:3 gives R/G=9.70, G/B=0.10 (G nearly noise-free) -> rejected; speckle:1 intensity slope +0.40 vs target +0.01 -> rejected; sb6 residual rgb_ratio 1.155 (<1.3). The run_full_analysis GAUSSIAN_YCrCb verdict (4/5 pairs) is the low-confidence gamma-suspect code path (cross_channel_corr>0.12 + residual_intensity_corr>0.15) polluted by blur/saturation structure, not a genuine YCrCb detection.

3) Noise severity = 4: target flat-patch amplitude is 1.18x R0's sev3 sim (sim/target 0.84-0.85 on R/G/B/Cr/Cb); sev4 sim matches 0.99/1.01/1.01/1.00/1.00 on pair0 and 0.94/0.98/0.99/0.99/0.98 on pair1. verify_signals: sev4 PARTIAL 5/6 (pairs 0/1/3), sev3 WEAK 2/6 (pair0), sev2 WEAK 1/6. The R0 variance_ratio mismatch (77%) resolves to 2.4% (0.9192 vs 0.9174) at sev4; mean_shift diff 0.0002.

4) Saturation = HSV2 (unchanged): run_full_analysis raw verdict proposed SATURATION_strengthen_sev5, but the deterministic 5-pair sweep clean->blur3->satN rejects it: HSV2 shift MAE 2.76, chroma|d| 0.09, dark-clip|d| 0.010, var|d| 0.097 vs HSV1 12.88/0.52/0.260/0.063, HSV3 6.30/0.32/0.226/0.146, HSV5 10.22/0.66/0.388/0.170. saturate_strengthen_YCrCb N=1..5 all 27.7-30.9 shift MAE -> subtype rejected. Brightness/gamma excluded (hue-dependent shifts match saturation clipping; equal-channel shift would be required).

5) Blur = gaussian3 (unchanged): under the corrected noise severity, spectral_slope diff 0.0005 (pair0) and Wiener kernel corr 0.9986-0.9987 (>0.85); glass_score 0.59/0.65 (pairs 1/3) remains the known glass-DT FP (R0: gaussian beats glass by 1.70 dB; flat-region mottling cannot come from pixel shuffle). Compression excluded (block_boundary 0.996-1.003, unique_G 236-247).
